audience.text: did you check on my goal
what happens if you break a vow

reply.line: Hail, and well met. Sir Vacant, of an order dissolved, keeping watch over the one promise nobody checked on. Speak your vow. The wax is warm, and I am listening.
Goals, in wax. Each one chat made, hung upon my chest and read aloud on the hour. The weight is considerable. I have grown to rely on it.
Water. A modest vow, nobly made. I shall set it in wax, between the stream goal and the unfinished novel. May it be kept, and may the visor widen.
I have checked. It is neither kept nor broken: it is simply waiting, as vows do. The wax has not cracked. That is, I am told, a good sign.
Is anyone in here? A fair question. There is a draught, a sense of duty, and a promise. It is more than most armour holds.
It is the hour. I will read the vows: nine are kept, four are pending, and one has been forgotten entirely. You know who you are. The visor notes it.
